All 4 findings were then fixed and independently re-verified by a SEPARATE verification subagent via targeted adversarial tests (out-of-repo rebuild, ZIP content inspection, forged self-reported capture_complete, bogus classification value), which reported all 4 genuinely resolved as of head 30b79b5c3a.

findings.title: build_zip_archive() crashed for any --output-dir outside --repo-root
findings.body: zip_path.relative_to(repo_root) raised an uncaught ValueError whenever the output directory wasn't a subpath of the repo root. Fixed with a try/except falling back to a bare basename in the sidecar. Independently re-verified: rebuild into /tmp exits 0 and shasum -c passes.

findings.title: Shipped ZIP did not contain PACKAGE_VALIDATION.json despite the package's own README advertising it as a deliverable
findings.body: build_zip_archive() ran before validate_chatgpt_project_sources.py ever executed as a separate script. Fixed by refactoring the validator into a callable run_validation() and having the assembler call it (writing PACKAGE_VALIDATION.json, failing closed on any gate failure) before zipping. Independently re-verified: unzip -l on a fresh build shows the file present with all_gates_pass:true.

findings.title: capture_complete trusted a self-reported flag instead of always recomputing it
findings.body: Fixed by always recomputing len(files)==changedFiles rather than trusting any self-reported field. Independently re-verified: a forged self-reported capture_complete=true with a real file-count mismatch was ignored, raising the FATAL error.

findings.title: No enum/allow-list validation on PR classification values
findings.body: Fixed with a VALID_PR_CLASSIFICATIONS enum check in build_pr_ledger_entries() that raises SystemExit on any unrecognized value. Independently re-verified: a scratch classifications file with a bogus value produced a clean FATAL exit naming the exact PR and value.
